motivation: T1 caller-authored variants improved some owner-unknown routes but deleted two raw-English successes. Test the smallest representation repair: preserve the caller's native query alongside derived lexical projections.
T2Construction: Variant 0 is always the exact raw user query.
Append authored variants in their already-frozen model output order.
Deduplicate exact strings without semantic rewriting.
Keep at most four total variants, matching Atlas first-look-many limit; therefore use raw + first three distinct authored variants when more exist.
No target, retrieval result, target rank or owner information may influence truncation or ordering.

preboundHypotheses.H1: If T1 loss was mainly caused by deleting the raw representation, T2 should recover the lost raw-success routes while retaining some T1 gains.
preboundHypotheses.H2: If T2 still loses a raw-success route, fixed-top-k merge/ranking or query-relative inspection geometry is the blocker; adding representations is not monotone under the current retrieval composition.
preboundHypotheses.H3: Chinese may benefit from English derived variants while retaining the native Chinese query as an explicit source representation, even if the raw Chinese channel contributes no lexical hit.

nonAdmissions: No change to Atlas ranking or inspect-candidate implementation admitted by this experiment.
